chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, so he said: There is no objection to it. I said: And the Magian woman? He said: There is no objection to it, meaning temporary marriage (mut'ah).

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is marriage to Jewish, Christian, and Magian women permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of marrying women of the Book (Jews and Christians) extends to Zoroastrians (Magians), a ruling often associated with their status as 'People of the Book' in Shia jurisprudence. He specifically notes that this applies to *mut'ah* (temporary marriage), highlighting the distinct application of this ruling in Shia fiqh compared to Sunni schools which generally restrict permanent marriage to them. This narration underscores the flexibility of marital laws regarding non-Muslim women within the Shia tradition, provided they are chaste.
